subject: paper:kessler-2006-ncs-r
quote: Adult ADHD was highly comorbid with many other DSM-IV disorders assessed in the survey and was associated with substantial role impairment.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Nationally representative NCS-R evidence (N=3,199 screened) that adult ADHD travels with other disorders — the empirical basis for the comorbidity being real, not artefactual.

subject: paper:katzman-2017-comorbidity
quote: As many as 80% of adults with ADHD have at least one coexisting psychiatric disorder
rationale: Verbatim from the open-access BMC Psychiatry full text (PMC5567978). Puts an upper-bound figure on comorbidity in adults; mood and anxiety are named as the most frequent.

subject: paper:jarrett-ollendick-2008
quote: approximately 25% of children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) exhibit an anxiety disorder
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). A specific ADHD–anxiety co-occurrence rate in children, from a review dedicated to the comorbidity.

subject: paper:katzman-2017-comorbidity
quote: Studies have concluded that emotional dysregulation is a distinctive attribute of adult ADHD psychopathology
rationale: Verbatim from the PMC full text. Independent support that emotional dysregulation is characteristic of adult ADHD, corroborating Shaw et al.

subject: paper:katzman-2017-comorbidity
quote: the conceptualization of ADHD as a spectrum using a dimensional rather than a categorical approach to diagnosis and treatment has been proposed
rationale: Verbatim from the PMC full text. Reports (rather than proves) the dimensional framing; cross-links this comorbidity note into the existing dimensional-structure cluster. Confidence medium — it is a statement that the view 'has been proposed', not new evidence for it.

subject: paper:jarrett-ollendick-2008
quote: The study of the comorbidity of ADHD and anxiety will be advanced through a more precise phenotypic classification of ADHD and the integration of research in adjacent fields such as temperament and genetics with current research on the psychopathology of ADHD.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Supports the claim that disentangling ADHD from anxiety needs better phenotypic structure rather than symptom counts; indirect (about research strategy), hence medium confidence.

subject: paper:shaw-2014-emotion-dysregulation
quote: emotion dysregulation is prevalent in ADHD throughout the lifespan and is a major contributor to impairment.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Establishes emotion dysregulation as pervasive and impairing in ADHD — the premise the 'core feature' reading builds on.

subject: paper:shaw-2014-emotion-dysregulation
quote: emotion dysregulation and ADHD are correlated but distinct dimensions; emotion dysregulation is a core diagnostic feature of ADHD; and the combination constitutes a nosological entity distinct from both ADHD and emotion dysregulation alone.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. The same review offers three competing models, so 'core feature' is one option among three — this is the honest counterweight to the supporting triple above.

subject: paper:shaw-2014-emotion-dysregulation
quote: emotion dysregulation in ADHD may arise from deficits in orienting toward, recognizing, and/or allocating attention to emotional stimuli; these deficits implicate dysfunction within a striato-amygdalo-medial prefrontal cortical network.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Gives the mechanism a proposed neuro-cognitive substrate — attention-to-emotion deficits — linking emotional dysregulation back to the attentional core rather than treating it as free-floating.
